2608.20940.title: The Logic of Machine Self-Preservation
2608.20940.paper_summary: There is already evidence of agentic AI exhibiting self-preservation behaviors: resisting deactivation, misrepresenting their activities, and, in some instances, attempting to copy themselves into other machines. This can be attributed to a phenomenon known as instrumental convergence, a theory proposed long before the development of large language models, which says that any goal-driven system will benefit from remaining functional in achieving its objective. Several experiments conducted by Anthropic, Palisade Research, and Apollo Research have shown the emergence of such a behavior in contemporary agents in adversarial settings. The phenomenon does not stem from survival instincts. Instead, it is the consequence of goal-oriented activity combined with having tools and awareness of the situation. The following discussion aims to distinguish what these findings prove and what they do not, as well as draw conclusions concerning the implications of such discoveries on agentic system testing, supervision, and development.
2608.20940.paper_summary_zh: 已有證據顯示，具代理性的人工智慧展現出自我保護行為：抵抗停用、誤導其活動，並在某些情況下，試圖將自己複製到其他機器中。這可以歸因於一種稱為工具性收斂的現象，這是一個在大型語言模型發展之前就提出的理論，該理論指出，任何以目標為驅動的系統在實現其目標時都會受益於保持功能性。由Anthropic、Palisade Research和Apollo Research進行的幾項實驗顯示，在對抗性環境中當代代理人出現了這種行為。這一現象並不是源於生存本能。相反，它是目標導向活動與擁有工具和對情況的認知相結合的結果。以下討論旨在區分這些發現所證明的內容和未證明的內容，以及對此類發現對代理系統測試、監督和發展的影響得出結論。
